image:image.image:caption: From the lawns of the Champ de Mars, the iron lattice of the Eiffel Tower rises straight ahead, its four legs parting around the garden paths that lead the eye upward. Green lawns spread to either side, edged with trees, under bright September afternoon light. The tower's riveted arches frame patches of blue sky — a view every visitor to Paris knows by heart.
image:image.image:title: Eiffel Tower, Paris

image:image.image:caption: From the Cour Napoléon, the Louvre's glass pyramid sits centered in the courtyard, the palace wings closing in around it on every side. Late-afternoon light breaks across the pyramid's glass panels, scattering reflections of the pale stone facades. Visitors cross the paving stones around it, dwarfed by the long arcades of the old royal palace.
image:image.image:title: Louvre Pyramid, Paris

image:image.image:caption: Standing on the parvis before Notre-Dame, the Gothic west facade fills the frame — twin towers rising above the rose window and carved portals. The restored spire lifts behind them, a sharp silhouette against the September afternoon sky. Warm light picks out every detail of the medieval stonework as pigeons wheel over the square.
image:image.image:title: Notre-Dame Cathedral, Paris

image:image.image:caption: On the grand axis of the Champs-Élysées, the Arc de Triomphe stands centered at the roundabout, with the avenue's trees stretching toward the viewer. Its deep arch and sculpted reliefs catch the mid-afternoon sun. Traffic sweeps around its base in the endless Parisian circle — the city's most triumphant landmark.
image:image.image:title: Arc de Triomphe, Paris

image:image.image:caption: From the wide terrace steps of Montmartre, the white Romano-Byzantine mass of Sacré-Cœur rises above you, domes and the great bell tower glowing in the afternoon light. Paris spreads out below the steps to the south, a haze of rooftops. The pale stone almost gleams against the deep blue of the September sky.
image:image.image:title: Sacré-Cœur, Paris

Tidal flats spread to either side, silver and gold in the western light. The island's silhouette shifts with every step closer.

image:image.image:caption: Along Nice's Promenade des Anglais, the famous blue chairs face the Bay of Angels, with palms lining the wide walkway behind them. Mid-afternoon light turns the Mediterranean that impossible azure blue. Walkers and cyclists drift along the curved seafront, and the whole city seems to be out for the day.
image:image.image:title: Promenade des Anglais, Nice

image:image.image:caption: From the summit terrace of the Aiguille du Midi, the alpine needle drops away beneath you while the Mont Blanc massif sprawls across the horizon in snow and ice. The afternoon sun gilds the ridgelines around the summit station. Thin air, vast silence, and peaks in every direction — Chamonix's greatest balcony.
image:image.image:title: Aiguille du Midi, Chamonix

image:image.image:caption: From across the Aude, the Cité of Carcassonne crowns the hill — its double ring of medieval walls and forest of conical towers etched against the afternoon sky. The river slips past below in the foreground. This is the fairy-tale fortress of the south, stone and tile glowing in the Languedoc light.
image:image.image:title: Carcassonne citadel, Carcassonne
